titleEn: What the Sea Brings, Show Dad First!

pages.text: "Wow, jelly!" Lolo in yellow boots crouched on the sand. Something soft, washed up overnight, gleamed. Lolo reached to grab it.
"Lolo, no!" Riri in her yellow hat quickly caught Lolo's wrist. Lolo wanted to find something nice on the beach to show Dad today. "Why not? It is so pretty!" Lolo pouted.
They ran to Dad the fisherman, who was tending his net. "Dad, there is shiny jelly over there!" Lolo pointed to the sand. Dad picked up a wooden stick at his feet.
Dad touched it only with the stick. Tap, tap. Squishy. "This is a jellyfish. Even out of the water, touching it can sting your hands." Lolo quickly tucked both hands behind their back.
"The sea leaves many things on the sand each night," Dad said. "Some must not be touched, so I always ask with a stick first." The stick seemed to greet things for Dad.
Dad taught them three rules. "One, do not touch unfamiliar things! Two, never put them in your mouth! Three, show Dad first!" Riri opened her fingers one by one to count. "One, two, three!"
Even seeing a branch with red berries, Lolo hid both hands behind their back. "What the sea brings, show Dad first!" Splashing along, Lolo ran to Dad.

Dad turned the branch over with his stick and smiled. "These berries washed down from the mountains. Eating them would hurt your tummy. Well done for coming without touching them." Lolo's cheeks grew pink, and shoulders lifted proudly.

From that day, Lolo tucked both hands behind their back at anything unfamiliar. One, do not touch! Two, do not put it in your mouth! Three, show Dad first! Whenever Riri found something unfamiliar, Lolo called first, "What the sea brings, show Dad first!"

When the sea breeze grew cool, Dad lifted Lolo onto his shoulders and held their hands. Some things the sea leaves must not be touched. "Dad, bring the stick tomorrow too. What the sea brings, show Dad first!"
